_status: Written before any policy was implemented and before any policy outcome was computed for any frozen scenario. The only market measurements taken were swap counts and RPC error counts.

venue.verifiedBy: live eth_call fee()/tickSpacing()/slot0()/token0()/token1()/decimals() on 2026-08-20; matches markout-study.md §2.1 verified independently on 2026-08-17

feeEnvelope._notFitted: Inherited from the AfterhoursFeeHook already deployed at 0xbCb4B7310BA36eA01f2A435A5D64C9b7953d8080 before this task existed. Not chosen after seeing any result.
feeEnvelope._sameForBothPolicies: Comparing a policy that may reach 2% against one capped lower would measure the cap, not the signal.

policies._sanityCheck: This is the pool's actual live behaviour, so its replayed fee revenue must reconcile with what the pool really charged.

policies._leakageRule: Any filing, news, rumour, event-type, market-hours or corporate-action input reaching this policy invalidates the comparison and must fail a test.

trigger._kNotChosen: k is a judgment call, so it is not chosen. Every event is reported at all three k values and the headline comparison uses all three. Reporting a single k would allow the strongest to be selected after the fact.

policies.response: step to maxFee, hold for widenDurationSec, decay linearly to baseFee over decayDurationSec
policies.indeterminateRule: Where a window has too few trades to estimate the reference statistic, record INDETERMINATE — never 'did not trigger'. Silence and a decision not to act are different findings.

policies.promotesVia: the frozen evidence graph plus market confirmation, reaching PROTECT
policies.thresholdOwnership: T1.2 and T3.3, not this document
bindingRules: thresholds must be frozen in versioned configuration before any scenario's market data is scored
the same frozen configuration applies to all four scenarios
the configuration version is recorded in every result row
if a threshold changes after any result is seen, every prior result is void and the benchmark is re-run and re-labelled
policies._gridRationale: See amendments AMD-001. Same discipline as VOLATILITY_ONLY's kGrid, and for the same reason.

eventSet._rule: No event may be added, dropped, or re-anchored after any result is seen.
eventSet._nullRowRule: Scenario A is reported as an evidence-path row with null economics. Never silently dropped, never imputed.
eventSet._dualBranchRule: Scenario C's TINJAU row is reported under both permitted branches (WATCH and PROTECT). Once T1.2 freezes the rule, the non-selected branch stays in the artifact as a disclosed sensitivity.

markout.horizonAnchor: the trade's own timestamp t*, not the anchor block
markout.haircut: 0.25 * feeRate * abs(inputUSD), where feeRate is the fee the policy under test would have charged on that swap
markout.coverageReporting: every horizon reports later_swap_count_by_h_* so a reader can see when it collapsed back to M_0
markout._reusedFrom: docs/buildx-orion-2026/outputs/05-build/markout-study.md §1.2–§1.3, so the two studies stay comparable

counterfactualLimitation.method: re-price the same observed swap sequence under different fee schedules
counterfactualLimitation.prescribedBy: tracker §0.13 ('identical trades, timestamps, initial liquidity, costs, and replay window')
counterfactualLimitation.falseAssumption: Changing the fee would have changed the trades. A pool charging 2% deters swaps a pool charging 0.05% attracts.

biasDirections.feeRevenue: OVERSTATED for any policy that raises fees — trades that would not have happened still pay
biasDirections.adverseSelectionBenefit: UNDERSTATED — informed flow the higher fee would have deterred is still present in the replay

counterfactualLimitation._honesty: The two biases push in opposite directions and the net sign cannot be determined from this data. Claiming the result is conservative, or that it is inflated, would be a guess. Flow elasticity to fee on this pool is unmeasured.
counterfactualLimitation._notFutureWork: Recorded as a known limitation, not as future work that softens the caveat.
bindingConsequences: fee revenue is reported separately from markout, never netted into one headline number
the phrase 'loss avoided' is gated by claimGate below
every published number carries basis: OBSERVED or COUNTERFACTUAL
TINJAU's observed testnet action and this mainnet replay are different pools and are never combined into one figure

reporting.primaryOutput: per-scenario, per-policy, per-k rows; aggregates come after, never instead
distribution: two most extreme swaps per scenario
reporting.tailConcentration: report the share of total markout from the single worst swap and from the worst 5%
reporting.completenessRule: the artifact must contain a row for every (scenario, policy, k) triple that was run
reporting._noHidingALoss: If VOLATILITY_ONLY matches or beats TINJAU at any k on any metric, that comparison is published with the same prominence as any favourable one.
reporting.sampleSizeDisclosure: The economic distribution rests on three scenarios, one asset, and windows in a market that is only weeks old. No sentence may imply a general result about tokenized equities.

requiresAll: the scenario has a non-null economic row
TINJAU beats both STATIC and VOLATILITY_ONLY at every k on the primary metric M_3600_LP
the margin exceeds the spread between the best and worst k for VOLATILITY_ONLY
the frozen threshold configuration was not modified after any result was seen
claimGate.onFalse: the artifact records which condition failed

conditions: TINJAU does not beat VOLATILITY_ONLY on M_3600_LP at one or more k
TINJAU promotes on scenario D, a routine Form 4, showing its materiality semantics are wrong
TINJAU reaches PROTECT on scenario A, violating the rumour invariant
TINJAU's advantage on scenario B disappears once the single largest swap is excluded
TINJAU's advantage exists only at one k for the volatility baseline
failureConditions.response: Any of these is reported as the finding. None is a reason to change the method.

amendments.change: Extend the k-grid discipline from the volatility baseline to Tinjau's own `minDrawdownBps`. T5 must report every event at 150, 200 and 300 bps rather than at 200 alone.
amendments.reason: The T3.3 agent was briefed to freeze thresholds blind, but the brief failed: a forked agent inherits the orchestrator's context, which already contained T3.2's measured drawdowns. The agent disclosed this rather than claiming blindness. `minDrawdownBps` is the single threshold separating the scenarios, so a reviewer cannot otherwise tell whether the result depends on it.
amendments.directionOfEffect: Adds disclosure only. A sensitivity grid cannot make a result look better than a single chosen value; it can only reveal fragility that a single value would have hidden.
amendments.effectOnClaimGate: Tightens it. `canClaimLossAvoided` already requires TINJAU to beat both baselines at EVERY k; the same must now hold across every drawdown threshold in the grid.
amendments.anchorOfTheChosenValue: 200 bps is anchored to the deployed hook's maxFee of 2% — invoking a 2% fee against a smaller dislocation is incoherent, since the defence would cost more than the exposure. That anchor is external to the four windows and predates any measurement of them.
